provincial.name: Social Assistance Program (Transitional Assistance + Extended Benefits)
provincial.who: Households whose total income is below the rate for their family type. Extended Benefits: clients certified blind, deaf or disabled by the Medical Advisory Board (18+, per policy manual).
provincial.what: Monthly income help for basics; Extended Benefits is the disability rate; includes health card, emergency fuel benefit, medical transportation.
provincial.notes: Main page does not name TAP/EBP; categories confirmed on 2021 reform page and policy manual (search snippet). Nurse practitioners can sign disability forms. Apply by phone 1-833-733-7835. Reform page fetched OK.

provincial.name: Disability Support Program
provincial.who: NB residents 19 to 64 with a long-term disability needing help to support themselves or take part in community; financial assessment sets contribution.
provincial.what: Personalized planning plus personal support, respite, daily-living training, disability transport, devices, residential services, Meals on Wheels.
provincial.notes: Contribution income-tested but eligibility is not. Excludes services other programs provide and addiction-only needs. Overlaps Self-Managed Support, Employment and Support Services.

provincial.name: Self-Managed Support
provincial.who: Clients of the Disability Support Program or Long-Term Care Program.
provincial.what: Monthly lump sum so client directs and hires own support providers (family allowed if not in same residence).
provincial.notes: Option inside DSP/LTC, not a stand-alone entry route; consider folding into DSP.

provincial.name: Employment and Support Services Program
provincial.who: People approved for and receiving Disability Support Program services; supported by one of 38 contracted non-profit agencies.
provincial.what: Life skills, community activities, job finding and inclusive paid work through agencies.
provincial.notes: Reached via DSP; call screening 1-833-733-7835.

provincial.name: Training and Employment Support Services (TESS) for Persons with Disabilities
provincial.who: New Brunswickers with a permanent physical, intellectual, psychiatric, cognitive or sensory disability; no need to receive income support.
provincial.what: Individually tailored help to take training, get, return to or keep a job.
provincial.notes: Apply at nearest WorkingNB office. Page does not state age limits or dollar amounts.

provincial.name: Family Supports for Children with Disabilities (FSCD)
provincial.who: Eligible families of children with a disability; page gives no criteria. Secondary sources: under 19, lifelong condition, not income-tested, but family contribution for those with means.
provincial.what: Funds unmet needs: equipment, medical transport, incontinence supplies, respite, home support, therapeutic recreation, health card if no coverage.
provincial.notes: Official page does not state age/income; age 19 cut-off from secondary sources (Migraine Canada, not official). Social worker contact 1-833-733-7835.

provincial.name: Mobility and Adaptive Equipment Loan Program
provincial.who: Social Development clients and dependents, or people with special health needs qualifying for assisted health care; valid Health Card; prescribed by OT or physio.
provincial.what: Free loan of basic/complex adaptive aids and manual/power mobility aids (run with Easter Seals NB recycling).
provincial.notes: Gated by Social Development health card (not open to all disabled people). Red Cross loans excluded as charity.

provincial.name: Orthopedic Program (Health Services)
provincial.who: Social Development clients and dependents with valid health card marked for supplementary/orthopedic, or special health needs; no other coverage.
provincial.what: Braces, supports, orthopedic footwear and insoles; adults shoes every 2 years, braces every 5.
provincial.notes: Same Health Services family as prosthetic, respiratory, ocular prosthesis pages (listed on hub; only orthopedic and ostomy fetched).

provincial.name: Ostomy/Incontinence Program
provincial.who: Social Development clients and dependents with white health card showing Supplementary or OS, or yellow card with Y; no other coverage.
provincial.what: Free ostomy, catheter and (limited) incontinence supplies paid monthly.
provincial.notes: Incontinence limited to wheelchair users, bedridden, ostomy/catheter users.

provincial.name: Prosthetic, Respiratory and Ocular Prosthesis Programs (Health Services)
provincial.who: Listed on hub as Health Services programs; eligibility assumed same Social Development health card basis but not fetched individually.
provincial.what: Coverage for prosthetic services, respiratory equipment/supplies, ocularist services.
provincial.notes: Individual pages (prosthetic.html, respiratory.html, ocular-prosthesis-program.html) NOT fetched; only hub confirmed. Fetch before ingesting.

provincial.name: Vehicle Retrofit Program
provincial.who: NB residents with a physical disability; also non-profits, municipalities, companies providing disability transport.
provincial.what: Up to 80% of eligible vehicle accessibility features, max $8,000; once every 8 years (organizations 5).
provincial.notes: No income test on page. Possible sales tax refund. Contact Ability NB 1-866-462-9555.

provincial.name: Accessible (Disabled) Parking Permit - New Brunswick
provincial.who: People with significant mobility impairment (cannot walk over 50 m unaided outdoors); signed by physician, OT, NP or physio.
provincial.what: Free permit and placard, apply at Service New Brunswick.
provincial.notes: Free. Expiry period not stated on page.

provincial.name: New Brunswick Prescription Drug Program (Social Development clients, seniors with GIS, special groups)
provincial.who: Valid NB Medicare card plus group: Social Development health card holders, seniors (65+) on GIS, nursing/residential facility residents, children in care and special-needs children.
provincial.what: Prescription coverage; Social Development clients pay $4 per adult / $2 per child prescription, capped $250 per family per year.
provincial.notes: Condition plans (CF, HIV, MS, transplant, growth hormone) out of scope. Special-needs children eligibility set by Social Development.

provincial.name: New Brunswick Drug Plan (income-based premium)
provincial.who: NB residents without other drug coverage who enrol; premium and copay set by family income (line 15000).
provincial.what: Drug coverage with sliding premium ($72/yr lowest tier rising to $2,896; copay 30% capped $5.25-$36).
provincial.notes: From Nov 1, 2026 lowest tier $89/yr (income <= $19,571 individual), top $3,087. Not free; subsidy-like sliding scale. Dependants under 19 pay no premium.

provincial.name: Healthy Smiles, Clear Vision
provincial.who: Children 18 or younger living in NB, no other dental/vision coverage, enrolled in CDCP, family net income within limit (e.g. 2 people $35,683; 4 people $50,463).
provincial.what: Basic dental and yearly eye exam, lenses and frames for children.
provincial.notes: Limits from June 2025 MBM; recheck yearly. Social Development child clients auto-transfer. Overlaps federal CDCP (requirement).

provincial.name: Preschool Autism Program
provincial.who: Child diagnosed with ASD, 5 or younger as of Dec 31, not in school, full-time NB resident (per 2020 handbook, not the page).
provincial.what: Publicly funded evidence-based ABA intervention through contracted agency.
provincial.notes: fetch returned page shell with no content; eligibility from search snippet of parent handbook and Oct 2025 guidelines PDF (not fetched). Provider naming conflicts (VIVA vs AIS).

provincial.name: Long-Term Care Program - Home Support (and nursing home subsidy)
provincial.who: Seniors 65+ with long-term functional needs after Social Development assessment; nursing home applicants 19+ assessed as needing that care; income/financial assessment for subsidy.
provincial.what: Home support (personal care, housekeeping, respite), day activity, nursing home and special care home subsidy.
provincial.notes: URL is a PDF from search results, NOT fetched; official topic page not located. March 2026 LTC plan changing home-care financial thresholds. Online estimator at socialsupportsnb.ca (not fetched).

provincial.name: Extra-Mural Program (EMP)
provincial.who: Any NB resident with valid Medicare card whose health needs can be met safely at home.
provincial.what: Publicly funded home healthcare: nursing, rehab, palliative, care coordination, in home, special care homes and nursing homes.
provincial.notes: Universal, not means- or disability-tested; page lists no fees. Include only if catalogue accepts universal health services.

provincial.name: Low-Income Seniors' Benefit
provincial.who: NB residents 60+ receiving federal GIS (65+) or Allowance / Allowance for the Survivor (60-64).
provincial.what: $629 annual payment (2026); apply by Dec 31.
provincial.notes: URL is the 2026 news release (annual); a stable program page exists at www2.gnb.ca/.../new-brunswick-low-income-seniors-benefit.html (seen in search, not fetched). Not disability-specific.

provincial.name: New Brunswick Child Tax Benefit and Working Income Supplement
provincial.who: Qualifying families with children under 18 (CCB administered); WIS needs earned income.
provincial.what: NBCTB up to $250 per child per year income-reduced; NBWIS up to $250 per family.
provincial.notes: Paid automatically with Canada Child Benefit. School Supplement ($100/child per search snippet) not on this page; unverified.

provincial.name: Portable Rent Supplement Program (persons with disabilities)
provincial.who: Individuals/couples able to live independently, with long-term impairment verified by health professional, CPP-D or Extended Benefits, or mental health client; adjusted income under ceilings ($45,000 1-bed urban).
provincial.what: Rent set at 30% of adjusted income; subsidy portable to any suitable unit.
provincial.notes: Apply Housing NB 1-833-733-7835. Also need housing-need test.

provincial.name: Rent Supplement Program
provincial.who: Low-income households under income ceilings chosen by demonstrated need (details from search snippet).
provincial.what: Rent reduced to 30% of adjusted household income in designated private units.
provincial.notes: Page NOT fetched, only search snippet; URL spelling 'suppplement' as published.

provincial.name: Residential Rehabilitation Assistance Program (RRAP) incl. accessibility modification
provincial.who: Homeowners/landlords with income at or below Housing Income Limits for repairs and disability accessibility modifications (search snippet).
provincial.what: Forgivable loan help for accessibility work and repairs; landlords up to $36,000/unit.
provincial.notes: Page not fetched; Housing Assistance for Persons with Disabilities page (services_renderer.19576) fetch returned no content. Homeowner accessibility caps unverified. Homeowner RRAP-Disabilities caps need check.

provincial.name: Ambulance fee exemption
provincial.who: Entitled Social Assistance recipients, GIS recipients, some Extra-Mural patients, nursing home residents with yellow health card.
provincial.what: No upfront ambulance bill ($130.60 standard NB resident fee).
provincial.notes: A benefit inside other programs; consider folding into Social Assistance and GIS records.

provincial.name: Student aid for students with permanent disabilities (NB integrated)
provincial.who: Students with a permanent or persistent/prolonged disability, verified by medical assessor.
provincial.what: Canada Student Grant for Students with Disabilities $2,800/yr; services and equipment grant up to $20,000/yr; 40% course load counts as full time.
provincial.notes: Federal overlap (already catalogued); no NB-only grant found. Page itself not fetched (search snippets).

municipal.name: Dieppe Accessible Transit (Transport adapte)
municipal.who: Dieppe residents who use a wheelchair permanently or have a significant persistent disability preventing safe transit use.
municipal.what: Subsidized door-to-door trips: $3 one-way in Dieppe, $6 to Moncton/Riverview; monthly trip allotment.
municipal.notes: Moncton/Riverview equivalents not found; Codiac Transpo covers Moncton, Dieppe, Riverview. 4-week processing. Page fetched OK.

municipal.name: Fredericton Para Transit
municipal.who: Registered clients with disabilities who cannot use fixed-route transit; city residents; age and finances not considered (2025 handbook per search).
municipal.what: Door-to-door service $3 cash or 10 tickets $27.50; attendant free.
municipal.notes: Register via Service Fredericton 506-460-2020. Handbook PDF unreadable via fetch. Low-income pass details unverified (only a 2019 news item); Transit Fare Assistance Program goes to agencies, not individuals.

municipal.name: Saint John Accessible Transit (formerly Handi-Bus)
municipal.who: People with disabilities unable to use regular Saint John Transit.
municipal.what: Specialized paratransit run by Independence Plus Inc.; $5.50 one-way per city FAQ (search snippet).
municipal.notes: Page is a news item; no registration or fare info on it. Phone 506-648-0609 from FAQ (not fetched). Find current Saint John Transit accessible page.
